item.description: The broker is its own published image; services talk to each other only through it; it picks the instance and runs the breakers. HA demo: `docker kill` one player copy, then run the last request: still all 200, and the broker log shows rerouted / TRIPPED.

item.name: Grade 6: subscriber queues (gateway → service) and topics (service → service)
item.description: Subscriber queue: the sender names the service, one copy answers, the sender waits. Topic: the producer does not know who listens; subscriptions come from the registration.

item.name: Subscriber queue: /queues/player/… → one copy answers
Queues are closed without the key (only the gateway has it)
The queues and their depth (bounded at 100)
Topics come from registration: Discovery /subscriptions
Publishing needs the key
Publish to a topic nobody wants: accepted, no subscriber
Level-up: 150 XP more (Player publishes player.leveled_up from its outbox)
The event went player → broker → game, and Game told the session

exec: pm.test('Game received it and told the session', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/received player\.leveled_up .*told 1 session/));

item.name: Broker log: published, stored for game, delivered over gRPC

exec: pm.test('stored for game', () => pm.expect(t).to.include('stored for game'));
pm.test('delivered to one game copy', () => pm.expect(t).to.match(/delivered to game at \S+:9082 \(gRPC\)/));

item.name: Grade 7: thread-per-request in the broker, list of topics
item.description: ThreadingHTTPServer: a new thread for every request, named req-<n>; HTTP/1.0 so one request per connection. Live demo outside Postman: hold 10 connections open and watch request_threads go 1 → 11 → 1.

item.name: GET /topics: every topic, its subscribers and counts

exec: pm.test('the level-up of grade 6 was delivered', () => pm.expect(lv.delivered).to.be.at.least(1));

item.name: /health counts the request threads (this one included)

exec: pm.test('this request has a thread of its own', () => pm.expect(h.request_threads).to.be.at.least(1));

item.name: Mark a request with an id
…its log line names its own thread
5 requests at once get 5 different threads

exec: for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) pm.sendRequest({url: pm.variables.replaceIn('{{brokerUrl}}/topics'), header: {'X-Request-Id': pm.collectionVariables.get('burst')}}, () => {});

item.name: The cap: at most 100 requests at once, the next one gets 429
gRPC side: a pool of threads rpc_<n>
Grade 8: gRPC between services; gateway closed to everything that is not a player's
item.description: Game ↔ Player and every event go over gRPC through broker:50051, forwarded undecoded. The gateway answers 404 to service-only routes even with a valid token.

item.name: Every instance registered a gRPC address
Game → broker → Player over gRPC (Get, SetPresence of the setup session)

exec: pm.test('gRPC calls forwarded to a player copy', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/\/player\.Player\/(Get|SetPresence) OK .*-> player at \S+:9081/));

Grade 9: durable queues, dead letter channel, its endpoint
item.description: Events are in SQLite (/data/broker.db, volume broker-data) before the ack, deleted after the subscriber acks. Durability demo outside Postman: docker compose stop game game-2 → level up → restart broker → start game.

item.name: The store survived restarts: opened from disk at start

exec: pm.test('SQLite store on the volume', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/message\(s\) waiting from before, \d+ dead letter/));

item.name: Dead letters need the key
Publish an event Game cannot read
Game rejected it: it is in the dead letter channel

exec: pm.test('the whole event is kept', () => pm.expect(d.event.payload).to.eql('not an object'));

item.name: Put it back on its queue
Retried, rejected again: a new dead letter for the same event

exec: pm.test('one dead letter, with a new id', () => { pm.expect(mine.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(mine[0].id).to.not.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('deadId'))); });

item.name: GET /topics counts waiting and dead
Unknown dead letter: 404
Grade 10: high availability, load-based balancing, Prometheus + Grafana + Loki
item.description: Load: the broker picks the copy with the fewest of its own calls in progress. HA demo outside Postman: docker pause / docker kill one player copy, then rerun grade 5's last request.

item.name: Load is measured per copy: broker_instance_in_flight

exec: pm.test('the broker tracks both player copies', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.result.length).to.be.at.least(2));

item.name: 10 calls at once are spread over both copies

exec: for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) pm.sendRequest({url: pm.variables.replaceIn('{{gatewayUrl}}/players?limit=1'), header: {Authorization: 'Bearer ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('token')}}, (err, res) => {
if (--left === 0) { console.log(count); pm.test('both copies took calls: ' + JSON.stringify(count), () => pm.expect(Object.keys(count).length).to.be.at.least(2)); }
